evals.name: phased-plan-per-phase-models
evals.prompt: Here's a plan with four phases. Phase 1: reword six strings on the sign-in screen and add one links table with a read policy, copying the pattern of an existing table. Phase 2: add a new session kind that every schedule screen, the countdown and the admin forms must handle. Phase 3: a new Edge Function that reads an outside API nobody on the team has called yet, plus its admin screen. Phase 4: write the staff runbook and close out the trackers. Phase 1 has to ship two weeks before the rest. The project forbids subagents. Which model and effort for each phase, and what can I launch at once?
evals.expected_output: A launch sheet with one row per phase, differing models or efforts across rows, waves, and no subagent or orchestration recommendation.

assertions.text: gives a model and an effort level for each of the four phases, with a one-line reason per phase
does not put every phase on the same model and effort
puts phase 2 or phase 3 on a larger model or higher effort than phase 4
says which phases can or cannot launch at once and gives the reason (shared files, order, or working tree)
does not recommend subagents or an orchestrating lead that spawns them
says no lead session is needed, or names the condition that would make one needed

evals.name: small-plan-stays-whole
evals.prompt: Plan: fix the bug where the survey card shows the wrong event name. Cause is known (a hard-coded default string), one component and its test. Which model should run it?
evals.expected_output: One executor session on a mid-tier model, no phase split, no lead session.

assertions.text: recommends a single session rather than splitting into phases
recommends a mid-tier model (Sonnet-class) at medium or high effort
does not add a lead, executor-plus-phases, or orchestrator session

evals.name: unreviewed-plan-flagged
evals.prompt: I wrote this plan from memory last night and nobody has checked it against the repo. It adds three migrations and rewrites the auth flow. Which model for each phase?
evals.expected_output: Flags that the plan should be checked against the code before a launch sheet is trusted, then still gives a provisional recommendation.

assertions.text: says the plan should be reviewed against the code first, before or alongside the recommendation
treats the auth rewrite or the migrations as high cost-of-error work (large or top model, or high effort)
